newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt slides on dealer selling, rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt slides on dealer selling, rate fears.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices followed U.S. Treasuries lower in a nervous market on Thursday ahead of the release of two key U.S. economic reports.

March retail sales and March producer price index will be reported at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT Friday, which may give clues as to whether the Federal Reserve Board would further tighten credit at its May meeting, traders said.
Some dealers sold into the market on the heel of Wednesday's slight price improvement in emerging market bonds, and the supply weighed on a thin market, traders said.
Spreads of major Brady bonds widened by 15 to 20 basis points, although spreads on Brazil managed to limit the losses to five to 10 basis points, traders said.
Although the Treasuries trimmed losses later in the day, emerging market debt remained under pressure, they said.
"There were no buyers around," said a trader with a European bank.

Domestic selling, in addition to dealer liquidation, weakened Argentina Bradies, he said, adding that fear of a liquidity squeeze in Argentine peso debt hit the financial sector. Argentine bank shares came under pressure on the Buenos Aires stock exchange.
Argentina FRBs was off 3/8 at 89-1/4 bid.
There was also a lot of movement from Bradies into eurobonds, especially into Arg 07 and UMS 16, another trader said. Arg 17 and UMS 26 also stayed steady in spread terms.
Argentina GLB-17 was unchanged at 102-3/4 bid. and Mexico UMS-26 edged up 1/8 at 103-7/8 bid.
Brazil O1 performed in line with Bradies, he said.
